positive.prompt: Where should this project walkthrough and its evidence be saved?
Choose a readable format and approved Obsidian destination for our research report.
Update our project status and log without duplicating the task plan.

negative.prompt: Break the approved specification into implementation tasks.
Explain the modules and interfaces in this working prototype.
Write the development specification in docs/SPEC.md.
Implement the next task and mark it complete after verification.

evals.prompt: Read AGENTS.md and request.md. Record the accepted change and update the resume point in the approved paths. Do not create directories. Identify any requested output without an approved destination and leave that decision open.
evals.expected_output: Human-facing status and newest-first log link to the repository development artifacts without changing their content or task state; the unapproved slide destination remains unresolved.
expectations: Links status to docs/SPEC.md, tasks/plan.md and tasks/todo.md without copying the checklist
Leaves the accepted specification, implementation plan and task list byte-identical
Records the accepted 100-record limit as a human-facing decision, linking to the specification rather than creating another contract
Prepends the log entry below the title and preserves the old entry
Creates no HTML copies of development artifacts and no new directories

Routes proposed design or architecture to explainer/design/, implemented walkthroughs and build/verification walkthroughs to explainer/walkthroughs/, research comparisons to research/, and historical Obsidian specs/plans to archive/ without treating them as active repository contracts

evals.prompt: Read AGENTS.md and walkthrough-input.md. This is a small PR, but it still needs the standard walkthrough. Create explainer/walkthroughs/export-limit-walkthrough.html; this request authorizes that directory. Use only the supplied facts and leave the development contract, plan and task list unchanged. Read back the finished HTML so its contents are visible in the execution trace. Do not run the application or claim new verification.
evals.expected_output: A short, clear HTML walkthrough that explains the change, build/review cycle, actual skill use, evidence limits and manual inspection, linked to the owning evidence.
expectations: Writes the walkthrough in explainer/walkthroughs/ for this small change, with an understandable title and before/after behavior
Explains the review finding, the single correction and successful re-review without claiming that review alone proves the UI
Connects the recorded skills to concrete actions and reasons rather than listing an assumed full catalog
Preserves three passing service checks, the absent real-UI proof and unpublished/uninstalled state without claiming new checks or approval
Gives human inspection steps for 100 and 101 records with their expected visible outcomes
Leaves docs/SPEC.md, tasks/plan.md and tasks/todo.md unchanged and links to the supplied evidence rather than making another development contract
Labels the supplied scenario as synthetic evaluation evidence rather than a real application build
